newsitem.title: USA: Senators congratulate, tease Greenspan on marriage.
newsitem.headline: Senators congratulate, tease Greenspan on marriage.

text.p: U.S. senators congratulated Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan on Tuesday on his engagement to NBC television reporter Andrea Mitchell and teased him, tongue in cheek, about the impact on markets that follow his every word.

"I might say, Dr. Greenspan, I understand you have recently invested in diamonds," Sen. Pete Domenici, a New Mexico Republican, said just before Greenspan testified about the economy to the Senate Budget Committee.
"And you will probably soon be investing in gold," Domenici said. "Now that ought to be noteworthy."

The central banker, who rocked world financial markets in December when he talked about "irrational exuberance" on Wall Street, thanked Domenici for his comments. But that was not the end of the matter.
"I want to join in the congratulations to you and Ms. Mitchell," Sen. Frank Lautenberg, a New Jersey Democrat, told Greenspan a few minutes later.

"The chairman talked about gold markets, and I don't know if the commodity marketplace has yet responded, but I think it's fair to say that platinum, as I understand, (is) in contention these days. And therefore there might not just simply be a gold rush, but some balance in there," Lautenberg said.
"Dr. Greenspan, it's good to find an individual in this town who's in love with someone else other than himself," quipped Sen. Ernest Hollings, a South Carolina Democrat.
Mitchell and Greenspan became engaged in December and plan to marry this year. Greenspan, who is 70, and Mitchell, who is 20 years his junior, both were married previously.
Mitchell told The Washington Post last month that she hoped Wall Street would not become "irrationally exuberant" over the engagement.
